# tritonctl floating-ip

Manage floating IPs

Alias: ip

Subcommands: list, show, create, delete, attach, detach

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl floating-ip list

List your floating IPs

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip list [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl floating-ip show

Show one floating IP

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Name, address, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl floating-ip create

Allocate a new floating IP in the project

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip create [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>`

- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--family <FAMILY>`: Address family to allocate from (one of: v4, v6; default: v4)

## tritonctl floating-ip delete

Delete a floating IP. It must be detached first

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Name, address, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails

## tritonctl floating-ip attach

Attach a floating IP to a NIC

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip attach [OPTIONS] --nic <NIC> <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Name, address, uuid, or prefix
- `--nic <NIC>`: NIC to attach to (name, MAC, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--instance <INSTANCE>`: The NIC's instance (name, uuid, or prefix). Needed to find a NIC by name or MAC

## tritonctl floating-ip detach

Detach a floating IP from its NIC

Usage: `tritonctl floating-ip detach [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Name, address, uuid, or prefix
